notes:
Account overview: Pivotal SupportWorks is a B2B SaaS contact center platform used by retail and finance customers. Currently runs agent-assist and automated summarization with a mix of OpenAI API + in-house model serving; experiencing throttling and inconsistent latency under marketing/spike events. Exploring Redwood as competitive replacement for support automation stack.

Key pain points: 
- Throttling from current vendor during promotional spikes; agents see 500-800ms extra latency leading to visible slowdown in agent UI.
- Current tool-calling (webhooks -> Salesforce Service Cloud) is brittle; need native function/tool-calling with strict at-most-once semantics.
- Summaries and suggested replies are sometimes hallucinated; need reliable reranking and eval hooks.
- Cost unpredictability during bursts; looking for predictable unit economics (dedicated or reserved pool).

Requirements discussed on call: 
- Latency SLO: 95p < 200ms for suggest endpoint (agent-assist); tail latency critical.
- Throughput: baseline 30 req/s for primary region, ability to burst to 300 concurrent suggestion sessions during campaigns.
- Embeddings + semantic search index: want efficient vector store integration; local KV-cache desirable to reduce token costs.
- Structured tool outputs: JSON schema enforcement for CRM updates.
- Security: Okta SSO/SAML, audit logging, KMS/HSM for keys, EU residency for EU customer tickets, 90-day retention default with options.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency dashboards, trace capture for failed suggestions.

Recent timeline & activity (bullets, CRM-style):
- 2024-11-15: Initial inbound via web form; AE Jordan Reyes assigned.
- 2024-11-28: Intro call (ff-id ff-4a7b9c) — product fit looks good, infra questions surfaced.
- 2024-12-10: Security questionnaire submitted; awaiting SOC2 evidence.
- 2025-01-06: Deep-dive demo with SE (Alicia) focused on function-calling + KV cache behavior.
- 2025-01-08: POC plan approved internally, POC kickoff scheduled (drive:/Pivotal/POC/...).
- 2025-01-10: Legal flagged EU residency requirement — slows procurement.

POC scope (agreed):
- Migrate agent-assist for a small pilot group (10% of agents) to Redwood Dedicated for 2 weeks.
- Run synthetic spike test (simulate 1k concurrent sessions) and measure tail latency, failover behavior.
- Validate function-calling to Salesforce (end-to-end) including at-most-once guarantee and structured outputs.
- Run reranking evaluation using 6 curated prompt sets; track QA/regression metrics.

Quotes / notes from stakeholders: 
- "If we still see tail spikes during promos, we can't move — must be rock solid." — VP Customer Ops.
- "Need deterministic billing during test so finance can greenlight Dedicated." — Head of Platform.

Open technical questions for SE: 
- How does Redwood handle KV cache persistence on node restart? warm cache behavior?
- What kernel/quantization recommendations for our model family (LLaMA-2 v13b variants)?
- SLA for burst capacity & automatic fallback to hosted models during Dedicated maintenance windows.

Next steps (short):
- Book load-test slot week of 2025-01-20 (owner: Alicia).
- Provide SOC2 + ISO summary to Pivotal legal (owner: Jordan).
- Draft SOW for Dedicated pilot; include explicit residency clause.

Internal deal notes (AE): 
- Likely close to mid-Q1 if POC shows stable tail latency and legal signs residency clause.
- Upside: customer will evaluate Redwood Optimize for batching/cost suggestions post-POC.
- Risk: procurement may push for pure hosted discount vs Dedicated — need to lock technical win first.
